1. Ni-tatnī, ‘striking downwards,’ occurs in the Atharvaveda^1
as the name of an unknown plant which was used as a means
of restoring the hair.
1) vi. 136; probably 137 also refers
to this plant. Cf. Kauṣītaki Sūtra,
xxxi. 28, with Caland's note in his
translation; Bloomfield, Atharvaveda,
61; Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 536, 537;
Whitney, Translation of the Atharva-
veda, 383.

2. Ni-tatnī is the name of one of the seven Kṛttikās in the
Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (iii. 1, 4, 1). See Nakṣatra.

Ni-tāna Māruta is the name of a man in the Kāṭhaka
Saṃhitā (xxv. 10).
